{"notes": "Visit 1 (1:30). Plan: fish. Everyone agrees on it and roles are mostly clear. Only Priya's and Leo's work is visible on the table; the rest is self-report.

PRIYA: Top line and start are connected to START. They run from about (29,4) round the dip at (23,8) to about (10.8,5.5), a long clean run with no visible gaps. She was ahead of her own estimate (said a fifth at 0:45). Clear and confident in delegating: told Leo to help Maya on the bottom line, and said she'd check the nose joint when her line gets there. Strong execution so far. Her line stops about 5 units short of where the nose should be.

LEO: Switched to the bottom line after Priya's delegation. Pale (not yet connected) dominoes run from about (6.2,13) to (15,14.5), which is steady and tidy. He asked what to do about overlap and proposed a split: he takes the whole bottom line, Maya takes the tail and fork. Good collaboration, with the overlap handled before it became a problem. Plans to check the nose join and tail later.

MAYA: Says she sketched the fish and rounded the nose on the pad to make the fall pass. I can't see any nose or tail dominoes yet, so this is unverified. At 1:00 she said she was laying the bottom line and tail, which overlaps with Leo. She raised the overlap herself and has not yet answered Leo's split. Good foresight on the sharp nose turn. Check next visit that the nose and tail exist.

TOM: Joiner/checker with no strokes of his own. Watching the nose corner as the likely break, a sensible instinct. No visible output yet, so I need to see him close gaps and flag problems. Watch for passivity.

TO CHECK NEXT: the nose join between the top and bottom lines, whether the tail gets built, and whether Maya and Leo settled their split."}
